summary: Underlying hardware is failing; the instance will be stopped on the retirement date.
steps: Confirm whether each instance is EBS-backed (data survives a stop/start) or uses instance store (data is lost).
Check whether the instance is behind a load balancer or Auto Scaling group; if so, replace it through the group instead.
For redundant production instances, stop and start them one at a time in a quiet period, checking health between each.
For single instances, schedule a short maintenance window before the retirement date.
Verify the application after restart; note that the public IP changes unless an Elastic IP is attached.
urgencyRule: Act before the retirement date. Production instances: at least several days before.

summary: A required update will be applied to the database during the maintenance window.
steps: Check whether the database is Multi-AZ. Single-AZ means several minutes of downtime; Multi-AZ means about 60-120 seconds of failover.
Take a manual snapshot before the window.
Tell dependent application teams and support about the expected downtime.
Consider applying the update earlier at a quieter time, or upgrading to Multi-AZ afterwards.
Make sure applications reconnect automatically after the restart.
urgencyRule: Prepare before the window. A single-AZ production database deserves extra attention.
typicalOwner: Application team that owns the database

summary: An AWS-side problem is causing Lambda errors or latency in a region. Customers cannot fix the root cause.
steps: Confirm impact in your own metrics (Lambda errors and throttles, downstream queue depth).
Make sure callers retry with exponential backoff and that failed events go to a dead-letter queue.
If you run multi-region, consider failing traffic over to a healthy region.
Tell stakeholders that the cause is on the AWS side and watch the Health dashboard for updates.
After recovery, replay any failed or dead-lettered events.
urgencyRule: Immediate monitoring while the event is open. Customers can only mitigate, not fix.
typicalOwner: Team that owns the affected function

summary: An IAM access key has been exposed publicly and may be abused.
steps: Immediately deactivate the exposed key, then delete it. Do not wait to investigate first.
Search CloudTrail for activity by that key since the exposure time.
Check for unauthorized resources: new EC2 instances, IAM users or roles, access keys and unexpected regions.
Create a replacement key if needed and store it in Secrets Manager, not in code.
Remove the secret from the repository and its git history, then add secret scanning to prevent a repeat.
urgencyRule: Treat as a security incident: act within the hour.
typicalOwner: Owner of the IAM user, with the security team

summary: A Lambda runtime version reaches end of support; functions keep running but get no security patches.
steps: List all functions using the deprecated runtime.
Update the code and dependencies for a supported runtime and test in a non-production environment.
Deploy the updated functions gradually, starting with the least critical.
Add a check to catch deprecated runtimes earlier next time.
urgencyRule: Plan before the deprecation date; low urgency for non-production.
